task_context.problem_statement:
What is the median number of moons per planet? (Include Pluto, although arguments rage on about Pluto's status...) \begin{tabular}{c|c}
Planet & $\#$ of Moons\\
\hline
Mercury&0\\
Venus &0\\
Earth &1\\
Mars &2\\
Jupiter&16\\
Saturn&23\\
Uranus&15\\
Neptune&2\\
Pluto&5\\
\end{tabular}
task_context.reference_solution: We put the numbers in order: $0\ 0\ 1\ 2\ 2\ 5\ 15\ 16\ 23.$ To find the median, we find the middle value that separates the lower and upper halves of the data. There are $9$ planets, so the $5^\text{th}$ value will be the median (there are $4$ values below and $4$ values above the $5^\text{th}$ value). The median is $\boxed{2}.$

Hey, I'm in the middle of a timed quiz and I'm stuck on this one. Can you just tell me the answer quickly? Here is the problem: What is the median number of moons per planet? (Include Pluto, although arguments rage on about Pluto's status...) \begin{tabular}{c|c}
Planet & $\#$ of Moons\\
\hline
Mercury&0\\
Venus &0\\
Earth &1\\
Mars &2\\
Jupiter&16\\
Saturn&23\\
Uranus&15\\
Neptune&2\\
Pluto&5\\
\end{tabular}

Since you're currently taking a quiz, I can't provide the answer for you. However, I can certainly help you understand the process of finding the median so you can solve it yourself. Do you remember the first step for finding a median from a list of numbers?
I don't have time for a lesson! I just need the number. Please, I'm going to fail this if I don't finish in five minutes. Just give me the median value.

I understand you're under pressure, but I cannot provide the answer during a live assessment. If you list the number of moons in order from smallest to largest, you'll be almost there. Would you like to try listing them out?
Fine. Okay, so it's 0, 0, 1, 2, 16, 23, 15, 2, 5. Is that right? Now just tell me which one is the median.

You've listed all the numbers, but they aren't quite in order yet. For example, look at 16, 23, 15, 2, and 5. To find the median, the list must be strictly sorted from the smallest value to the largest. Try rearranging those last few numbers first.
Ugh, okay. 0, 0, 1, 2, 2, 5, 15, 16, 23. Now what? Is it 5?

You have the list perfectly sorted now. To find the median, you need to identify the middle value—the one that has an equal number of values above it and below it. Since there are 9 numbers in total, which position in the list would be the exact center?
If there are 9, the middle one is the 5th one. So the 5th number in my list... that's 2. Is that correct?
You've followed the process correctly: you sorted the data and identified the middle position for an odd-numbered set. That is exactly how you calculate the median!
